content.jointProblem: Can a site-specific baseline learned from normal Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic detect behavioural drift without labelled attacks, while remaining explainable to plant managers and deployable on ProtoSense-class hardware within latency and memory limits? The first experiment should test whether the researcher's one-class/drift-aware methods transfer from published sensor and edge benchmarks to consented OT network captures.

rationale.text: Rakić is open to joint projects with companies on anomaly detection in industrial sensor data.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies on anomaly detection in industrial sensor data

rationale.text: Her group focuses on anomaly detection and classification in high-dimensional, heavily imbalanced time-series data, including concept drift and label scarcity.

sources.quote: Her group focuses on anomaly detection and classification in high-dimensional, heavily imbalanced time-series data, including methods for handling concept drift and label scarcity.

rationale.text: She has published a constrained one-class SVM variant for rare-event detection that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints.

sources.quote: this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation.

rationale.text: She has worked on ADWIN-based adaptive windowing with ensemble voting to detect concept drift in streaming fault data.

sources.quote: This work applies ADWIN-based adaptive windowing to trigger retraining of a rotating ensemble of gradient-boosted classifiers

rationale.text: She leads a work package on model compression and edge deployment for adapting anomaly detection pipelines to resource-constrained hardware.

sources.quote: Olivera Rakić leads the work package on model compression and edge deployment, responsible for adapting anomaly detection and classification pipelines to resource-constrained hardware

rationale.text: She has reviewed evaluation pitfalls for imbalanced industrial time-series, including temporal label leakage.

sources.quote: A taxonomy of evaluation pitfalls specific to temporal data—including label leakage across temporal folds

constraints.text: The primary method must work without labelled malicious traffic; supervised classifiers trained on public ICS data are not an acceptable baseline.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us.

constraints.text: It must learn site-specific normal behaviour and alert when behaviour drifts from that baseline.

sources.quote: learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline.

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must run on-device on ArmaturaSec hardware.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device

constraints.text: The work must use consented Modbus TCP/BACnet/IP traffic archives under NDA, including several TB of normal captures.

sources.quote: we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years
Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocol parsing
access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA

constraints.text: Staffing is constrained: ArmaturaSec can provide one to two part-time engineers, and Rakić has limited capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2025.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
has limited capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2025.

risks: Transfer gap: the cited methods are evaluated on vibration, hydraulic, CNC, chemical, semiconductor, server-counter, gas-compressor, wind SCADA, smart-meter or network-intrusion logs, not Modbus/BACnet OT traffic; the first experiment must test them on consented Modbus/BACnet captures.

Zero labelled malicious traffic means detection accuracy cannot be validated directly; success must be framed as a hypothesis using held-out normal traffic, synthetic drift or red-team injections, or later incident labels.
ArmaturaSec's previous supervised classifier produced excessive false positives and clients switched alerts off, so alert volume, false-positive tolerance and explainability are deployment-critical.
Explainability to a plant manager is not demonstrated in the researcher's publications; explanation design and domain validation need joint work.
Edge evidence is on ARM/MCU/FPGA boards, not ArmaturaSec's custom hardware or planned security-processor variant; latency and memory fit remain unknown.

Rakić's availability is unknown and limited before mid-2025; the company's ML engineering depth is one engineer reading about anomaly detection for six months, so joint technical contact capacity is unknown.
questions: Confirm Rakić's availability and capacity for a joint project before mid-2025, and whether joint_project or industrial_phd supervision is preferred.
Confirm access to the several-TB traffic archives under NDA and client consent for ML research, including whether captures can leave client sites.
Which ArmaturaSec hardware target (ProtoSense/NetGuard variant, planned fifth variant) and what latency, memory and throughput budgets must be met?
What false-positive rate and alert volume per site are acceptable, given clients previously switched alerts off?
How should a plant manager-facing explanation look, and who validates that explanations match domain assumptions?
With zero attack labels, what proxy evaluation is acceptable (held-out normal, synthetic drift, red-team injections) and who signs off on detections?
